chain.title: A Drawer Off Its Hinges
chain.desc: A wooden chest, rods and slabs; a standalone drawer that keeps its contents when broken and carried.

chain.title: Two Planks and a Promise
chain.desc: Crafted from oak planks around a wooden chest; a single compartment that holds far more of one item than a chest ever could.

chain.title: Split Down the Middle
chain.desc: The same planks-and-chest recipe arranged to yield one block divided into two independent compartments.

chain.title: Four Doors, One Block
chain.desc: The 2x2 arrangement of the planks-and-chest recipe, and the densest of the plain drawer forms.

chain.title: Shallow but Wide
chain.desc: Built with an oak slab instead of planks, giving a half-depth block that still exposes two compartments.

chain.title: Filling the Gaps
chain.desc: Oak planks and wooden rods form a blank facing block used to square off a wall of drawers.

chain.title: The Disguise Bench
chain.desc: Made from drawer trim, it lets a framed drawer take on the texture of any block you feed it.

chain.title: The Blank Slate
chain.desc: Wooden rods plus any drawer produce the blank template that every single upgrade in the mod is built on top of.

chain.title: Capacity, Tier One
chain.desc: Obsidian and a wooden rod on the upgrade template; the mod labels it Storage Upgrade (I), the lowest rung of the capacity ladder.

chain.title: Capacity, Tier Two
chain.desc: Copper ingots on the template give Storage Upgrade (II), the next step up in stacks held per compartment.

chain.title: Capacity, Tier Three
chain.desc: Iron ingots on the template give Storage Upgrade (III).

chain.title: Capacity, Tier Four
chain.desc: Gold ingots on the template give Storage Upgrade (IV).

chain.title: Capacity, Tier Five
chain.desc: Emeralds on the template give Storage Upgrade (V).

chain.title: Capacity, Tier Six
chain.desc: Diamonds on the template give Storage Upgrade (VI).

chain.title: The Last Rung
chain.desc: Netherite ingots on the template give Storage Upgrade (VII), the highest capacity tier the mod ships.

chain.title: Cut From Gold
chain.desc: A gold ingot and a gold nugget on an upgrade template; locks a drawer to its current item and is the parent of every other key.

chain.title: Nothing to See Here
chain.desc: An eye of ender combined with the drawer key; hides a drawer's item icons and count from anyone looking at the wall.

chain.title: Reading the Numbers
chain.desc: A writable book combined with the drawer key, toggling the printed item count on a drawer's face.

chain.title: Hands Off the Drawer
chain.desc: A hopper and wooden rods on the template, letting the drawer accept and emit items through automation.

chain.title: Pulling Things In
chain.desc: Copper and iron bars applied to a hopper upgrade so the drawer drags loose items toward itself.

chain.title: One Ingot, Nine Nuggets
chain.desc: Iron, stone and a piston around a full drawer; stores a block, its ingot and its nugget as one pooled quantity.

chain.title: The Switchboard
chain.desc: Diamonds, a comparator and stone around a drawer, turning an entire adjacent wall of drawers into one addressable inventory.

chain.title: An Extra Doorway
chain.desc: Gold, a comparator and stone around a drawer; displayed as Drawer Controller IO, it gives pipes a second access point onto the same network.

chain.title: Cutting the Tether
chain.desc: Ender pearls, redstone and wooden rods on the template, letting a drawer join a controller without touching the wall.

notes:
143 ids verified as assets/storagedrawers/models/item/*.json stems carrying a display name. Storage Drawers uses TWO name conventions: plain keys (block.storagedrawers.controller) and a COMPOSED one for every wood variant - block.storagedrawers.mat.<wood> ('Oak') x block.storagedrawers.type.<form> ('%s Drawers 2x2'). A naive item.<mod>.X / block.<mod>.X intersection verifies only 60 ids and silently discards all 84 per-wood blocks, which are genuinely registered (each has a blockstate and its own recipe). All 120 recipe results resolve to modelled items; nothing in the recipe graph is unmodelled.

KEY FINDING - the capacity ladder is NOT in material order. The lang file numbers them explicitly: obsidian=Storage Upgrade (I), copper=(II), iron=(III), gold=(IV), emerald=(V), diamond=(VI), netherite=(VII). Obsidian being tier one is counter-intuitive and worth gating on; the chain follows the lang numbering, not the material's usual tech position.

DROPPED - storagedrawers:controller_io. moddb lists it (2 packs) but it is NOT a registry name: there is no blockstate for it and it is absent from ModBlocks.class. It exists only as the legacy lang key block.storagedrawers.controller_io = 'Drawer Controller IO', which names the block actually registered as controller_slave (blockstate present, in ModBlocks.class, and the result of recipes/controller_slave.json). Quests must use storagedrawers:controller_slave. moddb also lists controller_slave separately (8 packs), so its two entries are the same block counted twice under one wrong name.
DROPPED - keybutton_personal: it has an item model and a lang key but appears in neither ModBlocks.class nor ModItems.class, and its blockstate file is misspelled 'keybutton_personel'. Orphaned asset, not obtainable.
DROPPED - 21 model stems with no display name: detached_drawer_full (the filled state of detached_drawer), the 12 keyring_* variants (registered in ModItems but named from whichever key they hold), tape, and four legacy upgrade_* / meta stems.

CONSENSUS CONFLICTS, recipe graph preferred in both cases:
1. moddb puts controller at pos 0.101, BEFORE upgrade_template at 0.110. The recipe graph disagrees sharply - controller costs diamonds plus a comparator, while upgrade_template is wooden rods plus any drawer. upgrade_template is placed first here, and it also gates every upgrade in the mod.
2. moddb puts magnet_upgrade at 0.208 but hopper_upgrade at 0.372. The recipe is a hard dependency - magnet_upgrade is crafted FROM a hopper_upgrade - so hopper_upgrade must come first. Chain order corrected.

The per-wood drawers are a wheel, never chain steps: 11 woods x 6 forms plus framed is 84 blocks that are the same item in a different plank. One wheel hangs off oak_full_drawers_4 with the other ten woods and the framed variant. Trims, slab-based half drawers in other woods, and the framed_* duplicates of controller and compacting drawers are deliberately left out entirely.

Two further moddb entries are covered only indirectly and this is deliberate: oak_half_drawers_1 and oak_half_drawers_4 (3 packs each) are the 1x1 and 2x2 forms of the half drawer, and the chain teaches that whole form once through oak_half_drawers_2 rather than spending three of its 24 slots on the same idea. magnet_upgrade_2 and magnet_upgrade_3 sit in the upgrade wheel instead of the chain for the same reason - they are more range, not a new mechanic.
